text:
oncall-bot: [ALERT] 10:45 UTC — deploy 2026-03-15T10:38Z increased 5xx on /v1/generate (p95 latency up). Severity: P1. Paging: sre-mia. Incident channel: #incidents.

sre-mia: I'm paged, joining. currently seeing 5xx tail at ~6% from 0.2% pre-deploy. Marker: rollout v2026-03-15-canary-3.

eng-alex: I rolled the canary. Noted a spike in upstream ECONNRESET and db connection churn right after deploy. Reproduced by replaying traffic to canary box.

infra-kate: infra view: LB healthchecks fine, but envoy upstream cluster shows increased 5xx to tasks serving canary. Connections per pod jumped x3.

ops-luis: Any DB migration with this release?

eng-alex: No schema changes. Only a small cache invalidation + new batching logic for long prompts. Might be amplifying connection reuse.

prod-tia: Customer impact: CS flagged Dedicated tenant "acme-marketing" seeing latency/timeouts. CS-Jordan is on it.

cs-jordan: Confirmed — multiple API errors reported by a small subset of customers on high concurrency. Triage: severity to customers is high for a few tenants.

sre-mia: We need a mitigation plan. Options: 1) automatic rollback (release-bot) 2) flip feature flag that disables new batching 3) siphon traffic away from canary at LB. What's fastest?

release-bot: Automatic rollback triggered by health-runner: attempt queued — status: failed (timeouts talking to canary-controller).

eng-alex: Hmm release-bot couldn't complete; controller API timed out because controller pod is overloaded.

infra-kate: I can scale controller to 3x, but that'll take 30s-60s. Meanwhile we can shift traffic out of canary at the proxy.

ops-luis: Suggestion: manual proxy route update to move 100% of canary traffic back to stable. Command: `lbctl route update --service=api --version=stable --weight=100`

sre-mia: Let's do both in parallel: infra-kate scales controller, ops-luis runs lbctl route update, eng-alex flips feature flag as fallback. Who's doing each?

infra-kate: Scaling controller now. `k scale deploy controller --replicas=3 -n release`

ops-luis: Executing route update now. `lbctl route update --service=api --version=stable --weight=100`

eng-alex: Preparing flag flip command: `ffctl set rollout-batching new-batching false --env=prod --actor=alex`

sre-mia: ops-luis, confirm when the route change is in effect and show traffic % to versions.

ops-luis: Route update applied. Current traffic: stable=100%, canary=0%. (Observed from LB)

sre-mia: Metrics: error rate dropping — 5xx from 6% -> 0.8% in 90s. p95 latency trending down. Good sign.

eng-alex: I'll still flip the feature flag to remove the risky batching: executing `ffctl set rollout-batching new-batching false` now.

release-bot: Controller scaled OK. Automatic rollback re-evaluated: now possible but manual rollback already completed by traffic shift.

prod-tia: CS update: Jordan, pls relay that we've diverted traffic and are disabling the new batching; ask customers to retry and we will follow up with RCA.

cs-jordan: On it. Messaging drafted. Will ping affected tenants now.

sre-mia: Verification checklist: 1) traffic to canary = 0% 2) 5xx < 1% cluster-wide 3) p95 latency within 10% of baseline 4) KV cache hit-rate recovering 5) no open DB locks. Mark progress as you check.

infra-kate: Checking DB locks — none reported. Cache warmup metrics show increased miss-rate but stabilizing.

eng-alex: Application logs show batcher exceptions stopped after flag flip. No lingering errors in canary pods.

ops-luis: Envoy metrics show no 5xx spikes on stable. SLO dashboards green.

sre-mia: Good. Let's hold for 15m to confirm stability. If green, we'll mark incident mitigated and start incident write-up and rollback postmortem.

prod-tia: Product wants a rollout pause until we analyze root cause. We'll gate future batching rollout behind a focused perf canary and load tests.

eng-alex: Root cause hypothesis: new batching increased concurrent upstream connections and exposed a connection pool limit scenario in the app->db path under high concurrency. Need to add connection pooling guard and backpressure.

infra-kate: Follow-ups for infra: increase observability on per-pod conn counts and add a circuit to the controller so release-bot can fall back to route update automatically.

sre-mia: Post-mitigation tasks: create runbook entry for when release-bot fails (manual LB siphon steps), add `ffctl` rollback shortcut to playbook, and schedule a canary stress test.

cs-jordan: Noted. Customer messages sent; one customer replied that errors subsided after ~3 minutes.

sre-mia: Marking mitigation: traffic siphon + flag flip succeeded. Monitoring for 20 more minutes then start postmortem. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

release-bot: Incident severity downgraded to P2 based on stable metrics. Logging timeline to incident system.

eng-alex: I’ll open an RFC to harden batching with connection limits and fail-safe bypass.

prod-tia: I'll coordinate the release pause and schedule a sync between eng, infra, and SRE tomorrow.

sre-mia: Closing channel for active ops; keeping thread for postmortem notes. If anything regresses, @sre-mia will re-open paging.
